newsitem.title: USA: Chase Telecom $160 mln junk bond deal postponed.
newsitem.headline: Chase Telecom $160 mln junk bond deal postponed.

text.p: Chase Telecommunications Inc's $160 million junk bond deal was indefinitely postponed late on Thursday as investors continued to turn a cold shoulder to startup telecom companies, according to a source close to the deal.
"It has been postponed due to difficulties in raising money for developmental (personal communications services)," the source said.
The deal failed to garner adequate investor interest even after it was restructured from units of zero coupon bonds with warrants to buy equity to a cash-paying, prefunded unit deal.

Price talk on the deal had initially called for senior discount notes with a 14 percent yield to maturity and 15 to 17 percent equity, then for 13-1/2 percent couponed seven-year senior notes and 20 percent equity, market sources said.

A heavy weighting of startup telecommunication credits turned detrimental to fund performance in more volatile markets of the past six months, players said, leaving a sour taste in the mouths of money managers. Further, the plethora of other types of credits currently asking for financing has allowed buyers to be more selective and stay fully invested at the same time.
"A lot of this deferred telecom paper hurt managers in March and then again in December so they're very wary of filling that basket again," the source said.

Michael Nechamkin, telecommunications analyst at BT Securities Corp, noted financial uncertainties of the C-block auction winners have hindered the cash raising efforts of not only Chase, but also NextWave Telecom Inc.
"Investors are very skeptical about about the C-block auction winners," Nechamkin said.

The Federal Communications Commission's C-block PCS license auction last year gave preference to entrepreneurial companies in hopes of broadening competition. Chase won licenses to provide PCS services primarily in the state of Tennessee, an area covering approximately 6.3 million population equivalents (POPs).

Chase was to receive financing from large PCS players including PrimeCo Personal Communications and Qualcomm Inc following the high-yield offering. The company has planned to launch its PCS service in the second quarter of 1998, a source told Rueters in May.
Chase did not immediately return phone calls.
